builders.angle: LITERAL. Work BRIEF-r22's fix list 1 to 4 in order and exactly as written, one wing at a time in the order the brief lists them, finishing each wing -- its signature object, its built walls, its darks, every room of it -- before starting the next. Item 4, the Heart's seam, is a bug: measure the cause, fix it, prove it. The literal angle won rounds 20 and 21.

THE OBJECT FIRST. The judges' deepest complaint is that each wing lacks the thing its name promises. Start from the four signature objects -- the maze wall, the range, the hidden door, the pumpkin -- and make each one a drawn object with a silhouette a child could name, its own shading and a contact shadow, at the scale of the Kid; then build each wing's room around its object. Items 2 and 3 follow from that; item 4 last.

THE SURFACE. Item 2 is your round: the cloud-texture-with-outlines material is the defect under all four wings. Build the house's surfaces -- clipped yew, soot brick, raised panelling, a mansion's courses and slates, ribbed pumpkin rind -- as real relief with light and the round-21 pen for their lines, and keep every dark deep. With the surfaces built, give each wing its objects (item 1) out of them. Item 4 last.
